subject: maths
title: Secants, Tangents and Their Properties
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Every answer shows the working. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: The number of tangents that can be drawn to a circle from a point inside it is —
questions.work: Every line through an interior point cuts the circle in two points, so it is a secant. No tangent is possible: 0.

questions.q: TP and TQ are tangents from T to a circle with centre O. If ∠POQ = 110°, then ∠PTQ is —
PQ is a chord of a circle with centre O and the tangent PR at P makes 50° with PQ. ∠POQ is —
CA and CB are tangents from C to a circle with centre O. If ∠ACB = 75°, then ∠AOB is —
The tangent from A to a circle is 24 cm and A is 25 cm from the centre O. The diameter of the circle is —
questions.work:
Tangent ⊥ radius: r² = OA² − AP² = 625 − 576 = 49 ⇒ r = 7 cm.
Diameter = 14 cm.

questions.q: From a point P, 5 cm from the centre of a circle, the tangent is 4 cm long. The radius is —
The number of tangents that can be drawn to a circle from an external point is —
questions.work: From a point outside a circle exactly two tangents can be drawn.

questions.q: From an external point P, secants PAB and PCD are drawn. If PA = 4 cm, AB = 6 cm and PD = 8 cm, then PC is —
questions.work:
PB = PA + AB = 10.
PA × PB = PC × PD ⇒ 4 × 10 = PC × 8 ⇒ PC = 5 cm.

questions.q: A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle with centre O. If ∠AOB = 125°, then ∠COD is —
questions.work:
For a quadrilateral circumscribing a circle, the angles subtended at the centre by opposite sides are supplementary: ∠AOB + ∠COD = 180°.
∠COD = 180° − 125° = 55°.

questions.q: The number of common tangents to two circles that do not touch and lie outside each other is —
questions.work: Two separate circles have 2 direct and 2 transverse common tangents: 4.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, match the columns or true/false).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) PT is a tangent at P to a circle with centre O and ∠QPT = 60° (PQ a chord); ∠POQ = ____. (ii) TP and TQ are tangents and ∠POQ = 110°; ∠PTQ = ____.
questions.answer:
(i) ∠OPT = 90°, so ∠OPQ = 30° = ∠OQP; ∠POQ = 180° − 60° = 120°. (The central angle is twice the tangent-chord angle.)
(ii) ∠PTQ = 360° − 90° − 90° − 110° = 70°.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) PAB is a secant and PT a tangent; PT = x cm, PA = 4 cm, AB = 5 cm, so x = ____. (ii) AB is a diameter, XPY a tangent at P and ∠PBA = 30°; ∠BPY = ____.
questions.answer:
(i) PB = 4 + 5 = 9; PT² = PA × PB = 36 ⇒ x = 6.
(ii) ∠BPY equals the angle in the alternate segment, ∠BAP. In △APB, ∠APB = 90° (semicircle), so ∠BAP = 180° − 90° − 30° = 60°. ∠BPY = 60°.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) PA and PB are tangents from P; the angle between OP and the chord AB is ____. (ii) X and Y are the points of contact of tangents from P with ∠XPY = 80°; ∠POX = ____.
questions.answer:
(i) OP is the perpendicular bisector of the chord of contact AB, so the angle is 90°.
(ii) OP bisects ∠XPY ⇒ ∠OPX = 40°; ∠OXP = 90° ⇒ ∠POX = 180° − 90° − 40° = 50°.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) PT = 6 cm, AB = 5 cm, PA = x (PAB a secant); x = ____. (ii) PQ is a tangent at Q, QOR a diameter and ∠POR = 120°; ∠OPQ = ____.
Fill in the blanks: (i) Chords AB and CD meet at P; PA = 4, PB = x + 3, PD = 3, PC = x + 5; x = ____. (ii) AB is a diameter, XBY a tangent at B and AC = BC; ∠CBY = ____.
questions.answer:
(i) PA × PB = PC × PD ⇒ 4(x + 3) = 3(x + 5) ⇒ 4x + 12 = 3x + 15 ⇒ x = 3.
(ii) ∠ACB = 90° and AC = BC, so ∠CAB = 45°. By the alternate segment theorem ∠CBY = ∠CAB = 45°.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks (any two): (i) Common tangents to two non-intersecting circles ____ (ii) Tangents at a point on the circle ____ (iii) Tangents at the ends of a diameter are ____ (iv) Common tangents to two intersecting circles ____.
questions.answer: (i) 4. (ii) one. (iii) parallel (both are perpendicular to the same diameter). (iv) 2.

sections.passage: The London Eye is a giant wheel shaped like a circle with centre O. From a point P on the ground, two straight cables PQ and PR touch the wheel at Q and R, and ∠QPR = 30°. S is a point on the major arc QR.

questions.q: The incircle of △ABC touches BC, CA and AB at D, E and F. Prove that AF + BD + CE = ½(perimeter of △ABC).
questions.answer:
Tangents from a point are equal: AF = AE, BD = BF, CE = CD.
Perimeter = AB + BC + CA = (AF + BF) + (BD + CD) + (CE + AE)
= (AF + AE) + (BD + BF) + (CE + CD) = 2AF + 2BD + 2CE.
So AF + BD + CE = ½ × perimeter.

questions.q: ABC is an isosceles triangle with AB = AC, and XAY is the tangent at A to its circumcircle. Show that XY ∥ BC.
questions.answer:
By the alternate segment theorem, ∠XAB = ∠ACB.
AB = AC ⇒ ∠ABC = ∠ACB. So ∠XAB = ∠ABC.
These are alternate angles made by AB with XY and BC, so XY ∥ BC.

questions.q: Two tangents PM and PN are drawn to a circle of radius 24 cm from a point P 25 cm from the centre. Find their lengths.
questions.answer:
∠OMP = 90°: PM² = OP² − OM² = 625 − 576 = 49 ⇒ PM = 7 cm.
Tangents from a point are equal: PN = 7 cm.

questions.q: PA and PB are tangents to a circle with PA = 14 cm. A third tangent CD touches the circle at E, with C on PA and D on PB. Find the perimeter of △PCD.
questions.answer:
CE = CA and DE = DB (tangents from C and from D).
Perimeter = PC + CD + PD = PC + CE + ED + PD = (PC + CA) + (DB + PD) = PA + PB = 14 + 14 = 28 cm.

questions.q: AB and AC are tangents from A to a circle with centre O and ∠BAC = 50°. Find ∠BOC.
Two concentric circles have radii 5 cm and 3 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle which touches the smaller circle.
questions.answer:
The chord touches the small circle, so the radius 3 cm is perpendicular to it at its midpoint.
Half-chord = √(5² − 3²) = √16 = 4 cm. Chord = 8 cm.

questions.q: Chords BA and DC of a circle meet, when produced, at P outside the circle. If PA = 4 cm, PB = 10 cm and PC = 5 cm, find CD.
questions.answer:
PA × PB = PC × PD ⇒ 4 × 10 = 5 × PD ⇒ PD = 8 cm.
CD = PD − PC = 8 − 5 = 3 cm.

questions.q: Prove that the tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are of equal length.
questions.answer:
Given: PA and PB are tangents from an external point P to a circle with centre O.
To prove: PA = PB.
Construction: join OA, OB and OP.
Proof: in △OAP and △OBP,
OA = OB (radii);
OP = OP (common);
∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° (a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact).
So △OAP ≅ △OBP (RHS), and PA = PB (corresponding parts). Proved.

questions.q: Chords AB and CD of a circle intersect at P inside the circle. If PA = (3x + 2) cm, PB = (3x − 2) cm, PC = 5⅓ cm and PD = 6 cm, find x.
questions.answer:
PA × PB = PC × PD ⇒ (3x + 2)(3x − 2) = (16/3) × 6 = 32.
9x² − 4 = 32 ⇒ 9x² = 36 ⇒ x = 2 (x must be positive).

questions.q: The angle between radii OA and OB of a circle is 130°. The tangents at A and B meet at T. Find ∠ATB and ∠ATO.
Chords AB and CD of a circle meet at P. If AP = x + 1, BP = x + 2, CP = x and DP = x + 4, find x.
SAT is the tangent at A to the circumcircle of △ABC. A line parallel to SAT cuts AB and AC at D and E. Prove that AB × AD = AC × AE.
questions.answer:
By the alternate segment theorem, ∠SAB = ∠ACB.
DE ∥ SAT, and AB is a transversal, so ∠ADE = ∠SAB (alternate angles).
Hence ∠ADE = ∠ACB.
In △ADE and △ACB: ∠ADE = ∠ACB and ∠DAE = ∠CAB (common).
So △ADE ~ △ACB (AA), giving AD/AC = AE/AB.
Cross-multiplying: AB × AD = AC × AE. Proved.

questions.q: PT is a tangent to a circle from an external point P. Chord AB, produced, meets TP at P. TA and TB are joined and TM bisects ∠ATB (M on AB). If ∠PAT = 40° and ∠ATB = 60°, show that PM = PT.
questions.answer:
By the alternate segment theorem, ∠PTB = ∠TAB = 40°.
TM bisects ∠ATB, so ∠ATM = ∠MTB = 30°.
∠PTM = ∠PTB + ∠BTM = 40° + 30° = 70°.
∠PMT is an exterior angle of △ATM: ∠PMT = ∠TAM + ∠ATM = 40° + 30° = 70°.
In △PTM, ∠PTM = ∠PMT, so PM = PT. Proved.

questions.q: Prove that a tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
questions.answer:
Given: a circle with centre O and a tangent XY touching it at P.
To prove: OP ⊥ XY.
Proof: take any point Q on XY other than P. Q lies outside the circle (a tangent meets the circle only at P), so OQ > OP (radius).
This is true for every point Q of XY, so OP is the shortest distance from O to XY.
The shortest segment from a point to a line is the perpendicular, so OP ⊥ XY. Proved.
